Email subject is fixed and sending has no confirmation step.
Clipboard failures are only shown as a message.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the inbox
sections.what: Brings in the notification data functions, the settings reader, the contact update helper and the link component.
sections.why: The inbox reads and changes notifications and contacts through these helpers.

sections.name: TYPE_COLORS
sections.title: Colors for each reminder type
sections.what: Gives each kind of reminder its own label color in the inbox.
sections.why: Lets the user spot the kind of reminder at a glance.
sections.watch_out: A new type with no color entry falls back to a grey color.

sections.name: TYPE_LABELS, EMAIL_TYPES, LINKEDIN_TYPES
sections.title: Labels and action groups
sections.what: Gives short names to each reminder type and sorts types into email and LinkedIn groups, which decide which send buttons appear.
sections.why: Likely reason: email and LinkedIn messages need different buttons.
sections.watch_out: A type left out of both groups gets only edit and done buttons.

sections.name: isDue
sections.title: Deciding which reminders are due
sections.what: Hides reminders already sent or dismissed, and hides those whose due time is still in the future.
sections.why: Keeps the inbox to actions the user can take now.
sections.watch_out: Reminders with no due time always show, and the comparison depends on consistent time text.

sections.name: NotificationBell (part 1)
sections.title: Inbox state and LinkedIn copy action
sections.what: Holds the open state, the list, the count, editing and status messages. Refreshes every minute and on change events. The LinkedIn action copies the drafted text, opens the contact's profile, and marks the item sent.
sections.why: Likely reason: the 1.5 second delay lets the user see the confirmation before the item leaves the list.
sections.watch_out: The browser can block clipboard copying, and a failure only shows a short error message.

sections.name: NotificationBell: if
sections.title: Sending the drafted email
sections.what: Checks that the email key, sender address and recipient exist, then sends the drafted message through the email route and marks the item sent.
sections.why: Checking first gives the user a clear reason instead of a failed send.
sections.watch_out: This sends a real email at once, with the fixed subject Hi and no confirmation step.

sections.name: NotificationBell (part 3)
sections.title: Inbox button and dropdown frame
sections.what: Shows the INBOX button with a count badge, and the dropdown panel with a title and close button. A full-screen layer behind the panel closes it when clicked.
sections.why: Likely reason: the full-screen layer lets a click anywhere outside close the panel.
sections.watch_out: The badge shows 9+ above nine items, so the exact count is hidden.

sections.name: NotificationBell (part 4)
sections.title: Each reminder in the list
sections.what: Shows each reminder's type label, title, recipient, body and drafted text. Shows an edit box while editing, a status line after an action, and No pending actions when the list is empty.
sections.why: Gives the full context before the user acts.
sections.watch_out: The drafted text box has a fixed height and scrolls, so long drafts are easy to miss.

sections.name: NotificationBell (part 5)
sections.title: Action buttons for each reminder
sections.what: Shows the buttons that fit the reminder: view the application, edit, save or cancel edits, copy and open LinkedIn, send now, open the mail app, and done.
sections.why: The buttons change so the user only sees actions that apply.
sections.watch_out: Dismiss in the header and Done at the bottom both hide the item without sending, and the screen does not explain this.

sections.name: inboxBtn
sections.title: Shared style for inbox buttons
sections.what: Defines the look of the small grey outlined buttons in the inbox.
sections.why: One shared style keeps the buttons consistent.

sections.name: inboxLink
sections.title: Shared style for inbox links
sections.what: Defines the look of the small accent-colored outlined links, such as view app and mail app.
sections.why: Same reason as the button style: a consistent look.

summary: The inbox dropdown. It lists due reminders and drafted messages, and lets the user copy a message to LinkedIn, send it by email, edit it, or dismiss it.
purpose: Shows what needs action now, such as messages to send or follow-ups to do.
why: Likely reason: messages are drafted ahead of time and need a person to send them, so the inbox keeps them in one place.
how: 1. Stored notifications are read and only due ones are kept. 2. The list refreshes every minute and whenever the stored data changes. 3. The count appears on the INBOX button. 4. Opening the panel shows each item with buttons that fit its type. 5. Copy and open LinkedIn copies the text, opens the profile, and marks the item sent. 6. Send now checks the email settings, calls the email route, and marks the item sent. 7. Dismiss or Done hides the item.
inputs: Stored notifications, the saved email key and sender details, and the contact record for each item.
outputs: The updated inbox count, copied text, an opened LinkedIn tab, sent emails, and items marked sent or dismissed.
risks: Email sends immediately with the fixed subject Hi and no confirmation step. The email key is sent from the browser to the server. Copy can fail if the browser blocks clipboard access. Unknown reminder types fall back to plain labels with no action buttons.
debug: If the count is wrong, check the due time and sent flags on the notification. If a send fails, read the status line under the item and check the email route's response. If LinkedIn copy fails, check the browser's clipboard permission. If an item has no action buttons, check its type in the type groups.
